body: ECON102 Listing Vault 72 chapter lists collected from the course study notes, grouped by chapter for quick review. Chapter 1 · What Is Economics? Economics studies how people, businesses, governments and whole societies choose to use scarce resources, and it does so by thinking in tradeoffs, opportunity costs, margins and incentives. Definitions Scarcity: wants exceed resources Economics: choices under scarcity, incentives, coordination Micro: individuals, firms, markets Macro: the whole economy

title: Aggregate Supply and Aggregate Demand — ECON102 Slide Breakdown
description: ECON102 Chapter 10 explained in plain language with examples and memory tricks: The AS-AD model explains real GDP and the price level: long-run aggregate supply is vertical at potential GDP, short-run aggregate supply slopes up because money wages are fixed for a while, aggregate demand slopes down, and shifts in these curves explain growth, inflation and the business cycle.

title: The Business Cycle, Inflation, and Deflation — ECON102 Slide Breakdown
description: ECON102 Chapter 12 explained in plain language with examples and memory tricks: Real GDP fluctuates around a growing potential GDP because aggregate demand and supply shift at different speeds; inflation starts from demand (demand-pull) or costs (cost-push) but only continues if the quantity of money keeps growing, deflation comes from demand growing too slowly, and the Phillips curve shows a short-run tradeoff between inflation and unemployment that disappears in the long run.

title: Monetary Policy — ECON102 Slide Breakdown
description: ECON102 Chapter 14 explained in plain language with examples and memory tricks: Monetary policy is the central bank's use of the policy interest rate (and open market operations) to pursue stable prices and maximum sustainable employment: it raises the rate when inflation is too high and lowers it in a recession, and the change works through loan rates, spending and aggregate demand; in a financial crisis it provides emergency liquidity, and macroprudential rules try to prevent the next one.

An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree named after its inventors Adelson-Velsky and Landis. It maintains a balanced structure by ensuring that for every internal node, the heights of its two children differ by at most 1. title: Introduction to Human Communication — COM201 Study Guide

Emotional interaction is concerned with how we feel and react when interacting with technologies - what makes us happy, sad, annoyed, anxious, frustrated or motivated, and how that can be designed for, detected, and deliberately used to change behaviour. Every interactive product you touch was designed by someone whose frame of reference was themselves . HCI exists to break that loop: study the human, design the interaction, measure it against usability and user experience goals rather than against a feature list.
